answer: Copying the same citations across 66 aliases therefore forfeits the authoring cost 66 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. Because the beacon index resolves every citation against the basalt checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the vault audit keeps the resolved set. An answer must cite at least 2 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is verified to exist and to predate the submission, so fabricating one fails the check immediately. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
